preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner to call setVault function

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, call setVault() with address(0) as the argument. This will set the vault to zero address, breaking the mint functionality since onlyVault modifier will reject all calls (including legitimate ones) because no one can be the zero address. This is a denial-of-service attack on the minting capability.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The setVault() function in VaultOwned contract lacks zero address validation. While transferOwnership() has require(newOwner_ != address(0)), setVault() has no such check. This allows the owner to set vault to address(0), which breaks the onlyVault modifier since no caller can be address(0). This permanently disables the mint() function, causing a denial-of-service attack on the token's minting capability.
attempts.attack_strategy: Impersonate the contract owner and call setVault(address(0)) to set the vault to zero address. This demonstrates the missing validation vulnerability and shows that minting becomes impossible.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Get the current owner of the contract. 2. Impersonate the owner using vm.prank(). 3. Call setVault(address(0)) on the target contract. 4. Verify that vault() now returns address(0).
